neighbours.label: the last stem token of a plural common noun whose plural ending is a separate token, after a modifier (run|ways, catalyst|s, lantern|s, German …system|e, …lamp|en). Singulars and single-token plurals stay quiet.
fire: The new airport will have three parallel runways.
Platinum and nickel are widely used industrial catalysts.
The street was decorated with hundreds of red paper lanterns.
The city draws its water from two mountain reservoirs.
The paint is thinned with strong chemical solvents.
Für die Nachtwanderung brauchen wir helle Taschenlampen.
Die Gärtnerei nutzt moderne automatische Bewässerungssysteme.
Certain rare metals turn out to be excellent catalysts.
quiet: The new airport will have one long runway.
Platinum is a widely used industrial catalyst.
The street was decorated with hundreds of red paper flags.
The city draws its water from two mountain lakes.
The paint is thinned with a strong chemical solvent.
Für die Nachtwanderung brauchen wir eine helle Taschenlampe.
Die Gärtnerei nutzt ein modernes automatisches Bewässerungssystem.
Certain rare metals turn out to be excellent magnets.

short: stem before a split-off plural ending
notes: Top examples are German, Russian and English plural nouns caught one token before the ending (Bewässerungss|ystem|e, автоб|ус|ов, run|ways, mo|ths, catalyst|s); the - pole is plural surnames (the Clooneys, the Millers). Splits checked with the tokenizer. Probes were uneven: run|ways 0.44, catalyst|s 0.53, …system|e 0.52, lantern|s 0.15-0.33, sol|vents 0.27, …lamp|en 0.24, reservoir|s 0.22, but mo|ths 0.18, fern|s 0.06, dialect|s 0.05, sed|atives 0.01; singulars 0.00-0.02. The median fire may fall under 0.20. The singular 'Bewässerungssystem' keeps the stem token and drops only the ending, which is the hardest near miss here.
